mcqs.stem: Best guess: which offering can use general advertising and still be exempt from registration?

choices.explanation: Most private placements prohibit general solicitation.
Correct. Rule 506(c) permits general solicitation when all purchasers are accredited and verified.

mcqs.explanation: Rule 506(c) permits general solicitation when all purchasers are accredited and verified.

mcqs.stem: A company wants to raise $8 million from any investors within 12 months without registering. Which exemption fits best?

choices.explanation: Correct. Up to $10 million in 12 months.

choices.text: Rule 147 intrastate, with investors in several states

mcqs.explanation: Rule 504 covers offerings up to $10 million in a 12-month period.

mcqs.stem: Which tax does the employee **not** pay?

choices.explanation: Correct. FUTA is paid only by employers.

choices.text: Additional Medicare tax on high wages

mcqs.explanation: FUTA is an employer-only tax.

mcqs.stem: Which security is exempt from registration under the 1933 Act?

choices.text: Common stock of a manufacturer sold to the public
choices.explanation: Must be registered unless an exemption applies.

choices.text: Bonds of a private company maturing in 5 years
Six-month commercial paper for current operations
choices.explanation: Correct. Short-term notes (≤ 9 months) for current transactions are exempt securities.

mcqs.explanation: Short-term notes (≤ 9 months) for current transactions are exempt securities.

mcqs.stem: Under Rule 506(b), how many nonaccredited investors may participate?

choices.explanation: Correct. 506(b): unlimited accredited investors plus up to 35 sophisticated nonaccredited investors.

mcqs.explanation: 506(b): unlimited accredited investors plus up to 35 sophisticated nonaccredited investors.

mcqs.stem: A director buys company stock on March 1 and sells it at a profit on July 15 of the same year. What rule applies?

choices.text: None, because insiders may trade freely
The director must register the shares first

choices.explanation: Correct. Purchase and sale within 6 months.

mcqs.explanation: §16(b): officers, directors, and 10%+ owners disgorge profits from purchases and sales within 6 months.

mcqs.stem: Which report does a public company file to disclose a significant event such as a change in auditors?

choices.explanation: Correct. Form 8-K reports current events (auditor changes, acquisitions, bankruptcy).

mcqs.explanation: Form 8-K reports current events (auditor changes, acquisitions, bankruptcy).

mcqs.stem: An employer's state unemployment credit is the full 5.4%. What is the FUTA tax for an employee earning $45,000?
Under ERISA, which vesting schedule is permitted for employer contributions to a 401(k) plan?

choices.explanation: Too long for defined contribution plans.
Ten years is far beyond the maximum.
Correct. Defined contribution plans: 3-year cliff or 2-to-6-year graded vesting.

mcqs.explanation: Defined contribution plans: 3-year cliff or 2-to-6-year graded vesting.

mcqs.stem: An employee is injured on the job due to the employer's negligence. What is the employee's usual remedy against the employer?

choices.text: A negligence lawsuit for unlimited damages
choices.explanation: Workers' comp is the exclusive remedy.
Correct. Workers' compensation is no-fault and the exclusive remedy against the employer (with limited exceptions).

mcqs.explanation: Workers' compensation is no-fault and the exclusive remedy against the employer (with limited exceptions).

mcqs.stem: Which employer must offer COBRA continuation coverage?

choices.text: Any employer with a group health plan
choices.explanation: Small employers under 20 employees are exempt under federal COBRA.

choices.text: One with 20 or more employees and a group plan
choices.explanation: Correct. COBRA applies to employers with 20+ employees; coverage generally lasts 18 months.

choices.text: Only public companies with health plans
Only employers with 50 or more employees

mcqs.explanation: COBRA applies to employers with 20+ employees; coverage generally lasts 18 months.

mcqs.stem: Which individual qualifies as an accredited investor?

choices.text: A person with a $900,000 net worth, including her home
choices.explanation: Must exceed $1 million excluding the primary residence.

choices.text: Income of $250,000 in each of the last two years, same expected
choices.explanation: Correct. Individuals qualify with income over $200,000 ($300,000 joint) or net worth over $1 million excluding the primary residence.

choices.text: A person with a $150,000 annual income
Any investor with a college degree in finance

mcqs.explanation: Individuals qualify with income over $200,000 ($300,000 joint) or net worth over $1 million excluding the primary residence.

mcqs.stem: Under the FLSA, a nonexempt employee paid $20 per hour works 46 hours in one week. What are her gross wages for the week?

choices.explanation: Pays straight time for all hours.

mcqs.explanation: Overtime at 1.5 × the regular rate for hours over 40: 800 + 6 × 30 = **$980**.

mcqs.stem: Under the Affordable Care Act, an employer is an applicable large employer subject to the employer shared responsibility provisions when, in the prior year, it averaged at least:

choices.text: 20 or more employees of any kind, the same threshold as COBRA
choices.explanation: 20 employees is the COBRA threshold, not the ACA test.
Correct. Applicable large employers averaged 50 or more full-time employees (30+ hours a week), counting full-time equivalents.
The threshold is 50, and part-time hours count through FTEs.

choices.text: 50 employees working at least 40 hours per week
choices.explanation: Full-time means 30 or more hours a week for the ACA.

mcqs.explanation: ACA §4980H applies to applicable large employers: 50 or more full-time employees (30+ hours) including FTEs, measured over the prior year.

mcqs.stem: Under the ACA, when does an applicable large employer owe an employer shared responsibility payment?

choices.text: Any employee declines the employer's health plan in any month
choices.explanation: Declining offered, affordable coverage triggers nothing.

choices.text: A part-time employee buys coverage on a marketplace exchange instead
choices.explanation: Only full-time employees receiving a premium tax credit count.

choices.text: The employer has fewer than 50 full-time employees during the year
choices.explanation: Smaller employers aren't subject to the employer mandate.

choices.text: A full-time employee gets a premium tax credit on an exchange
choices.explanation: Correct. The §4980H payment is triggered when at least one full-time employee gets a premium tax credit because coverage wasn't offered, affordable or of minimum value.

mcqs.explanation: The penalty applies only if a full-time employee receives a premium tax credit for exchange coverage.

mcqs.stem: A company pays a designer by the project. The designer uses her own equipment, sets her own hours, invoices several other clients and can earn a profit or suffer a loss. Under the IRS common-law test, the designer is most likely:

choices.text: An independent contractor, reported on Form 1099-NEC
choices.explanation: Correct. She controls how and when the work is done and bears financial risk, so she is a contractor; no withholding or employer FICA applies.

choices.text: An employee, because she works for the company regularly
choices.explanation: Regularity alone doesn't make a worker an employee.

choices.text: An employee, because the company decides which projects to offer her
choices.explanation: Choosing what work to buy isn't control over how it is done.

choices.text: A statutory employee subject to FICA but not to income tax withholding
choices.explanation: Statutory employees are narrow categories (e.g., certain drivers and agents).

mcqs.explanation: The common-law test weighs behavioral control, financial control and the relationship of the parties. Here each points to an independent contractor.

mcqs.stem: Under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act's anti-bribery provisions, which payment by a U.S. company is permitted?

choices.text: A payment to a foreign official to win a government contract
choices.explanation: Paying a foreign official to obtain or retain business is prohibited.

choices.text: A payment through a local agent, knowing it will reach an official
choices.explanation: Indirect payments made with knowledge are equally prohibited.

choices.text: A small facilitating payment to speed up a routine permit
choices.explanation: Correct. Facilitating payments for routine governmental action are an exception to the anti-bribery provisions.

choices.text: A gift to a foreign party official to influence a pending regulation
choices.explanation: Officials of foreign political parties are covered too.

mcqs.explanation: The FCPA prohibits giving anything of value to foreign officials to obtain or retain business, directly or indirectly. Facilitating payments for routine, nondiscretionary governmental action are excepted.

mcqs.stem: Who pays the federal unemployment (FUTA) tax?

choices.explanation: Correct. FUTA isn't withheld from employees.

mcqs.explanation: FUTA is imposed solely on employers.

mcqs.stem: An employee earns $50,000 in 2025. What is the employer's share of FICA tax?
mcqs.explanation: The employer pays 6.2% Social Security plus 1.45% Medicare on wages up to the wage base: 7.65% × $50,000 = $3,825.

mcqs.stem: An employee earns $250,000 in 2025. What is the employer's Medicare tax on these wages?

choices.explanation: Correct. 1.45%; the employer doesn't match the 0.9% add-on.

mcqs.explanation: The employer pays 1.45% on all wages; the 0.9% additional Medicare tax is the employee's alone.

mcqs.stem: A company's CFO willfully uses withheld payroll taxes to pay suppliers instead of the IRS. What is the CFO's exposure?

choices.text: A penalty of 100% of the unpaid trust fund taxes
choices.explanation: Correct. The §6672 trust fund recovery penalty applies.

choices.text: None, because the company owes the tax
A penalty of 25% of the unpaid amount
Only the employer's share of FICA

mcqs.explanation: §6672: a responsible person who willfully fails to collect or pay over withheld taxes is liable for 100% of the trust fund amount.

mcqs.stem: Which categories of evidence does the IRS use to decide whether a worker is an employee?

choices.explanation: Correct. The three categories of the common-law test.

mcqs.explanation: The IRS groups the common-law control factors into behavioral control, financial control and the relationship of the parties.

mcqs.stem: How may a business ask the IRS for a determination of a worker's status?

choices.explanation: Correct. Form SS-8 requests a status determination.

mcqs.explanation: Form SS-8 is used to request an IRS determination of worker status.

mcqs.stem: An employer has 40 full-time employees and 20 part-time employees who each work 60 hours a month. Is it an applicable large employer under the ACA?

choices.text: No, it has only 40 full-time employees

mcqs.explanation: ALE status counts full-time employees plus FTEs (part-time hours per month ÷ 120); 50 or more makes an ALE.

mcqs.stem: Under the ACA, a full-time employee is one who averages at least:
mcqs.explanation: For the ACA, full-time means an average of at least 30 hours per week or 130 hours per month.

mcqs.stem: Which companies are subject to the FCPA's accounting provisions?

choices.explanation: The accounting provisions apply to issuers.
Correct. They must keep accurate books and adequate controls.

mcqs.explanation: The FCPA's books-and-records and internal-control provisions apply to issuers.

mcqs.stem: A U.S. company's payment to a foreign official is lawful under that country's written laws. What is the effect under the FCPA?

choices.explanation: Written local law provides a defense.
That exception is for routine acts.
Correct. Payments lawful under written local law are a defense.

choices.text: It must be disclosed to the SEC

mcqs.explanation: The FCPA provides an affirmative defense when the payment was lawful under the written laws of the foreign country.

mcqs.stem: An employer has 10 employees who each earn $20,000 and gets the full 5.4% state credit. What is its FUTA tax?
mcqs.explanation: Net FUTA is 0.6% of the first $7,000 of each employee's wages.

mcqs.stem: An employee earns $180,000 in 2025. The Social Security wage base is $176,100. What is the employee's share of FICA?

choices.explanation: Social Security stops at the wage base.

mcqs.explanation: Employee FICA = 6.2% of wages up to $176,100 plus 1.45% of all wages.

mcqs.stem: For 2025, at what amount must a business generally file Form 1099-NEC for payments to an independent contractor?

choices.explanation: Correct. The threshold rises to $2,000 in 2026.

mcqs.explanation: For 2025, Form 1099-NEC is required for nonemployee compensation of $600 or more.

mcqs.stem: An employee is fined for violating the FCPA. May the employer pay the fine for him?

choices.explanation: Correct. Employers can't pay individuals' FCPA fines.

mcqs.explanation: The FCPA prohibits an employer from paying fines imposed on individuals for violations.

mcqs.stem: The IRS reclassifies a company's contractors as employees. The company consistently treated them as contractors, filed 1099s and relied on industry practice. Which relief may apply?

choices.explanation: Correct. It may bar employment tax assessments.

mcqs.explanation: Section 530 can relieve a business from employment taxes if it had a reasonable basis and treated workers consistently.

mcqs.stem: A full-time life insurance salesperson works for one company but is treated as a contractor for income tax. How is she treated for FICA?

choices.text: As a statutory employee subject to FICA
choices.explanation: Correct. Certain workers are statutory employees for FICA.

choices.text: As a contractor exempt from FICA

mcqs.explanation: Statutory employees, such as full-time life insurance agents, are subject to FICA withholding.

mcqs.stem: A waiter receives $500 of cash tips in a month. What must he do?

choices.explanation: Correct. Tips of $20 or more a month must be reported.

choices.text: Report only on his own return

mcqs.explanation: Employees must report monthly tips of $20 or more to the employer for withholding.

mcqs.stem: In 2025 a family pays its nanny $3,000 (the household employee threshold is $2,800). What applies?

choices.text: Nothing, as she's a household worker
The family owes FICA on her wages
choices.explanation: Correct. Wages over the threshold are subject to FICA.

choices.text: Only income tax withholding is required

mcqs.explanation: Household employers owe FICA when cash wages to an employee reach the annual threshold.

mcqs.stem: An employer reported $60,000 of employment taxes in its lookback period. What deposit schedule applies?

choices.explanation: Correct. Over $50,000 in the lookback period.

mcqs.explanation: Employers with more than $50,000 of taxes in the lookback period deposit semiweekly.

mcqs.stem: A bookkeeper signs payroll checks but had no authority over which bills got paid and didn't know taxes went unpaid. Is she liable for the trust fund recovery penalty?

choices.text: Yes, as anyone who signs checks

choices.explanation: That isn't what the rule says.

choices.text: Only if she's a corporate officer

mcqs.explanation: §6672 applies to responsible persons who willfully fail to pay over withheld taxes.

mcqs.stem: An applicable large employer offers coverage to only 80% of its full-time employees, and one full-time employee gets a premium tax credit. What results?

choices.explanation: Correct. It failed to offer coverage to 95%.

choices.text: A penalty only for that one employee
choices.explanation: 4980H(a) is based on all FT employees.

mcqs.explanation: An ALE that fails to offer coverage to 95% of full-time employees owes §4980H(a) if any full-time employee receives a PTC.

mcqs.stem: A privately held U.S. company with no SEC-registered securities bribes a foreign official. Which FCPA provisions apply?

choices.explanation: Correct. Domestic concerns are covered; accounting rules apply to issuers.

mcqs.explanation: The FCPA's anti-bribery provisions cover domestic concerns; the books-and-records and controls rules cover issuers.

mcqs.stem: A U.S. company pays a foreign sales agent a large commission while ignoring clear signs the agent bribes officials. Can the company be liable under the FCPA?

choices.text: No, it didn't pay the bribe
No, the agent is a foreigner
Only if it was told directly

mcqs.explanation: Under the FCPA, knowing includes awareness of a high probability and conscious disregard.

mcqs.stem: An employer in a FUTA credit reduction state pays state unemployment tax in full. What is the effect?

choices.explanation: Correct. Credit reduction states have unpaid federal loans.

choices.text: No effect on FUTA at all

mcqs.explanation: In credit reduction states, employers get less than the full 5.4% credit, so net FUTA exceeds 0.6%.

mcqs.stem: By when must an employer furnish Forms W-2 to employees and file them with the SSA?

choices.explanation: That was the old paper filing date.

mcqs.explanation: Forms W-2 must be furnished to employees and filed with the SSA by January 31.

mcqs.stem: What does the Fair Labor Standards Act mainly govern?

choices.explanation: Correct. The FLSA sets wage and hour rules.

mcqs.explanation: The FLSA sets the federal minimum wage, overtime pay and child labor rules.

mcqs.stem: What does Form I-9 verify?

choices.explanation: Correct. I-9 verifies identity and work authorization.

mcqs.explanation: Employers use Form I-9 to verify each new hire's identity and eligibility to work in the U.S.

mcqs.stem: What is the effective FUTA tax rate after the maximum state unemployment credit?
mcqs.explanation: FUTA is 6.0% of the first $7,000 of wages, less a credit of up to 5.4%, for 0.6%.

mcqs.stem: A company raises $30 million from 200 accredited investors after advertising online and verifying each investor's status. Which exemption fits?

choices.explanation: Online advertising to anyone isn't intrastate.
Correct. 506(c): general solicitation, unlimited amount, all purchasers accredited and verified.

mcqs.explanation: 506(c): general solicitation, unlimited amount, all purchasers accredited and verified.

mcqs.stem: Which employee benefit is required by federal law for an employer with 60 employees?

choices.text: A defined benefit pension plan for all employees
Up to 12 weeks of unpaid FMLA leave
choices.explanation: Correct. FMLA applies to employers with 50 or more employees.

choices.text: Two weeks of paid vacation each year
choices.explanation: Federal law doesn't require paid vacation.

mcqs.explanation: FMLA applies to employers with 50 or more employees.

mcqs.stem: A company treated a worker as an independent contractor, but the IRS determines the worker was a common-law employee. Which consequence most likely follows for the company?

choices.text: The worker alone owes all of the unpaid Social Security and Medicare taxes
choices.explanation: The employer is liable for the employer share and the failure to withhold.

choices.text: Nothing, as long as the company issued the worker a Form 1099-NEC each year
choices.explanation: A Form 1099 doesn't change the worker's status.

choices.text: It owes the unpaid employment taxes, plus penalties and interest
choices.explanation: Correct. Reclassification makes the company liable for FICA, FUTA and income tax withholding (at reduced §3509 rates if the error wasn't intentional).

choices.text: The company may deduct the worker's pay only in the year of reclassification
choices.explanation: Reclassification doesn't change when wages are deductible.

mcqs.explanation: Misclassifying an employee exposes the employer to unpaid FICA and FUTA, failure-to-withhold liability (reduced under §3509 for unintentional errors), penalties and interest.

mcqs.stem: The FCPA's books-and-records and internal accounting control provisions apply to:

choices.text: Issuers whose securities are registered with the SEC
choices.explanation: Correct. The accounting provisions apply to issuers; the anti-bribery provisions reach a wider group.

choices.text: Every U.S. business that makes any sale to a foreign customer
choices.explanation: Foreign sales alone don't trigger the accounting provisions.

choices.text: Only foreign companies operating with offices in the United States
choices.explanation: They apply to issuers, U.S. or foreign, with SEC-registered securities.

choices.text: Tax-exempt organizations that receive foreign government grants
choices.explanation: Exempt organizations aren't the target of the accounting provisions.

mcqs.explanation: Issuers must keep books and records that accurately reflect transactions and maintain a system of internal accounting controls.

mcqs.stem: An employer qualifies for the full 5.4% state credit against FUTA. What FUTA does it owe for an employee paid $30,000 in 2025?

choices.explanation: That is 6.0% before the state credit.
That is the credit, not the tax.

mcqs.explanation: FUTA: 6.0% of the first $7,000 of each employee's wages, less a credit of up to 5.4% for state unemployment taxes, for a net 0.6% ($42).

flashcards.back: (b): no general solicitation; up to 35 sophisticated nonaccredited. (c): general solicitation; all accredited and verified.
Officers, directors, and 10%+ owners return profits from trades within 6 months.
